nodes.label: New Colors Go Into tokens.md First (BLESS decision)
nodes.rationale: Legitimate new colors go into tokens.md FIRST, then the deliverable — never the reverse. If the gate blocks a build, fix the colors; never widen the matcher or edit the lint to pass. Prevents mechanical gates from being bypassed by loosening enforcement.
nodes.norm_label: new colors go into tokens.md first (bless decision)

nodes.label: Failure #1: Parquet Footer Cache OOM (run_258112875741742)
nodes.rationale: Databricks disk cache (spark.databricks.io.cache.enabled=true) caches Parquet footer metadata; scanning 7.8B rows accumulated ~800MB+ on /local_disk0, filling disk at gate validation. Fix: disable disk cache — zero perf cost since workload doesn't benefit from footer caching (random access pattern).

nodes.label: Failure #2: Shuffle Spill OOM (run_583603715501680)
nodes.rationale: max_parallel=4 concurrent table writes on unpartitioned 5.86B-row source overwhelmed shuffle temp space; problem scales with parallelism (unlike Failure #1 which scales with data volume). Fix: max_parallel=2 halves peak shuffle temp pressure, trading 1-2h runtime for reliability on shared cluster.

nodes.label: Failure #3: S3 IAM Permissions (run_913314832159321)
nodes.rationale: Cluster IAM role lacked read access to s3://sasmaster-2026/temp/ prefix for job submission file, failing job at startup HEAD validation. Fix: fallback to /dbfs/tmp path with confirmed access; rule — never use S3 for job submission files on shared clusters without pre-verifying IAM.

nodes.label: Unpartitioned Sources Are the Bottleneck (Key Insight)
nodes.rationale: All Nielsen laapp_prod tables are heap scans (unpartitioned at source), so parallelism limits are driven by source table row count, not date range/lookback window — increasing lookback saves write time but not read time, since full table is always scanned.
nodes.norm_label: unpartitioned sources are the bottleneck (key insight)

nodes.label: amrld_time_period_view v1→v2 Migration Decision
nodes.rationale: v1 has stale data (last write 2026-06-18, versions being deleted); v2 shows active writes through 06-18. Catalog inspection is definitive; schema identical (AMRLD-flat family, BROADCAST_DATE watermark). Rollback: uncomment v1/comment v2 in manifest.py if Nielsen reverts.

nodes.label: Token-Inverted-Index Fuzzy Matching
nodes.rationale: Naive O(n) rapidfuzz scan over 4M+ IMDB titles caused a 36-minute hang; inverted index reduces candidate set to <500 per query, cutting runtime to ~4 minutes for 4,263 rows.

nodes.label: CONTEXT-VALIDATOR Gate
nodes.rationale: Score=1.0 exact matches are not safe without context validation — generic titles like 'Yachting' (1897 film) or 'Poker' (1913 film) would poison the spine without this gate.

nodes.label: Rule 1: Set-based writes, never row-by-row
nodes.rationale: 903K-row fusion write via executemany took ~15 hours; the same write set-based took seconds.

nodes.label: Rule 3: Cardinality discipline, dedup at source
nodes.rationale: A single non-deduped join blew the episode build to 84M–126M rows vs ~5.3M expected (~15–24x).
nodes.norm_label: rule 3: cardinality discipline, dedup at source

nodes.label: Rule 4: Circuit-breakers inside the loop
nodes.rationale: Post-loop breaker let build run to 126M rows before a human killed it; moved inside the batch loop it stops at ~10M.

nodes.label: DATA-009 TV Series Spine Parity Fix Suite
nodes.rationale: OFFSET pagination on a live subquery JOIN re-evaluates and re-inflates on every conn.execute() call; materializing once into a TEMP TABLE before batching fixes the fan-out.

nodes.label: Reconcile Formula Double-Counting Fix
nodes.rationale: Reanchored rows carry original imdb_id so appear in both 'covered' and 'cohort_excs' buckets; must build _covered_ids and subtract it from each reason-code bucket before summing to avoid double-counting.

nodes.label: Mint-Verify-Then-Store Doctrine
nodes.rationale: Mint a dedicated least-privilege user, prove read works, prove write DENIED, then hand the credential to the external store — generalizes to any third-party secret store.

nodes.label: OPUS Upsert Three Gates (upsert-never-replace, EIDR-first, no grain explosion)
nodes.rationale: Two writers hitting the same eidr_id keys concurrently produces last-write-wins non-determinism the doctrine bans, so REPAT must settle the baseline before OPUS enriches on top.
nodes.norm_label: opus upsert three gates (upsert-never-replace, eidr-first, no grain explosion)

nodes.label: Watermark Pattern for Large Writes
nodes.rationale: Dynamic partition overwrite with a watermark floor means completed partitions never re-processed on restart; without it a restart forces a full history re-run.

nodes.label: Two-Regime Cluster Doctrine
nodes.rationale: Incremental weekly runs use autoscale spot workers; full backfills use fixed on-demand-driver clusters with maxFailures=8 to survive spot preemption on long runs.

nodes.label: Rule 11: Pre-write purge for first-run tables
nodes.rationale: Multiple cancelled runs leave stale parquet files at the S3 prefix; validate_write() reads ALL of them, inflating the count and causing a false ABORT — amrld_household_data had 564K stale files from 3 prior runs.
nodes.norm_label: rule 11: pre-write purge for first-run tables

nodes.label: Rule 13: %%MARKER%% template style
nodes.rationale: {TABLE} placeholders in generated Python scripts require {{TABLE}} escaping that conflicts with real Python braces (set comprehensions, dicts); %%TABLE%% + .replace() avoids escaping conflicts entirely.

nodes.label: Reach (of Campaign) Metric
nodes.rationale: Sum of weights of distinct PIDs exposed to Campaign promos; varies by frequency because PIDs below the given watch-frequency threshold are excluded. 1+ reach includes anyone who watched at least once.

nodes.label: Impressions Metric
nodes.rationale: Sum of PID weight counted once per promo viewing, so a PID's weight is added repeatedly for repeated exposures within the Campaign.

nodes.label: Conversion Metric
nodes.rationale: A PID converts if it watched at least one promo AND watched >=1 minute of the actual premiere airing, indicated by the program's premiere date/time.

nodes.label: In-Tab Qualifier Rule (75%/single-day)
nodes.rationale: For projects >7 days, a PID must be in-tab 75% of project duration days to qualify; for projects <=7 days, being in-tab even one day qualifies. Age-changing PIDs must satisfy the 75% rule within their demo's age boundary.

nodes.label: Quintile Assignment Method
nodes.rationale: Qualified PIDs ranked descending by minutes watched, in-tab days, and average weight, then split into 5 equal quintile segments.

nodes.label: Quad Assignment Method (Gold/Silver/Occasional/Lite)
nodes.rationale: Two-parameter grid (percentage of viewing days x average minutes watched per viewing day) buckets qualified PIDs into Gold/Silver/Occasional/Lite at the >=40%/>=25min thresholds.

nodes.label: Quad Assignment Threshold Table
nodes.rationale: Explicit 4-row table: Gold >=40% viewing days & >=25 min; Silver >=40% & <25 min; Occasional <40% & >=25 min; Lite <40% & <25 min.

nodes.label: Brand-Asset / Brand-Product-Asset Structure Model
nodes.rationale: Content assets are modeled as Brand(Franchise)->Asset(Theatrical/TV) while CP (consumer products) assets are modeled as Brand(Franchise)->Product(w/ Attributes)->Asset, unified via an IP-Name-PK-to-Asset-PK mapping so both content and merchandising rights can share a common IP identity while carrying different attribute structures.

nodes.label: Cost Leadership vs Differentiation Strategy Matrix
nodes.rationale: Classic Porter generic-strategies framework (cost leadership / cost focus / differentiation / differentiation focus, scoped by narrow vs broad competitive scope) applied to assess whether RSG is 'stuck in the middle' rather than committed to one advantage source.

nodes.label: RSG Media Product Lineup (RightsLogic/PlanIt/AdVant/Promo)
nodes.rationale: RightsLogic = Content & IP rights management; PlanIt & AdVant = advertising planning; Promo = planning/scheduling (sourced from A&E) plus optimization (sourced from VMN); Analytics Services spans AdVant, PlanIt and Promo — defines RSG's core enterprise-software portfolio as of this document.

nodes.label: Rights Maturity Model Assessment
nodes.rationale: Structured client-discovery framework covering system usage, information entry/integration gaps, reporting maturity, content-portfolio value tiering (Rising Star/Evergreen/Dog/Question Mark), rights-usage KPIs, risk/misuse exposure, and degrees of automation/AI adoption across the value chain — used to score a prospective RightsLogic client's rights-management maturity.

nodes.label: AppDynamics (Performance Monitoring)
nodes.rationale: Used by RSG Media's Performance Team to identify the longest user journeys, flag any page response over 10 seconds, and trend-analyze usage patterns to find optimization opportunities and follow up on clients' SRM implementations.

nodes.label: Asset Shell Creation/Management API Use Cases
nodes.rationale: Nine numbered use cases scoping a RightsLogic API demo for VICE: create asset shells per asset type, manage inter-asset relationships, add/update metadata, create/associate versions, create deal shells, associate agreements, update deal/media rights terms, update financials (payments & revenue share), and list maintenance.
nodes.norm_label: asset shell creation/management api use cases

nodes.label: RightsLogic API (ASP.Net/C#, SOAP+JSON)
nodes.rationale: Out-of-the-box APIs organized by RightsLogic module; GET/POST semantics with soft-delete on record removal; JSON or XML responses over HTTPS; OAuth bearer-token auth against the Security module; logged/timestamped transactions; supports SSO via Active Directory/LDAP/SAML; example GetRightsAvailability call aggregates cleared vs holdback rights across deals and returns FULLY CLEARED / PARTIALLY CLEARED / NOT AVAILABLE.

nodes.label: XPeranto (RSG ETL Tool)
nodes.rationale: Proprietary high-transaction/high-speed batch-file ETL tool offered as an alternative to API-based integration, supporting Oracle, SQL Server, Sybase, DB2, FileMaker Pro, Access, and Excel imports.

nodes.label: CRMS (Contractual Rights Management System)
nodes.rationale: RightsLogic-based system Rogers deployed to capture contractual rights/restrictions for licensed Linear, PPV, and VOD assets; bidirectionally integrated with Ericsson's CMS across three interfaces (IF-1 linear-services XML ingestion, IF-2 adhoc VOD API requests, IF-3 rights/restrictions push back to CMS), with a defined exception-code taxonomy (INT_EX_001 through at least INT_EX_016+) for troubleshooting file-format, matching, and parameter errors.

nodes.label: RightsLogic
nodes.rationale: RSG Media's flagship end-to-end rights management platform: Asset Maintenance, Rights In/Out, Program Planning & Scheduling, Finance, Report Builder — positioned as the 'single truth' system of record across the content lifecycle to eliminate siloed databases and manual rights tracking.

nodes.label: Report Builder
nodes.rationale: Self-service reporting module (later powered by TIBCO Jaspersoft in v4) letting business users build ad-hoc reports without IT, addressing the recurring client pain point of manual report reformatting.

nodes.label: I-CON / ICON Intelligent Contract Interpretation
nodes.rationale: Hybrid human/machine-learning contract ingestion approach (started March 2018, using Google TensorFlow) meant to replace tier-1 deal analysts by training on RSG legal team's contract corpus, reducing deal backlog and human interpretation error.

nodes.label: Media Mantra
nodes.rationale: Analytics-as-a-Service offering that loads, cleanses & normalizes 1st/3rd-party audience data via machine-learning matching (98% match rate), then activates it into dashboards, apps and a schedule-optimization recommendation engine that predicts audience flow between programs.

nodes.label: AdVant Promo Optimization
nodes.rationale: Machine-learning promo scheduling tool using Nielsen respondent-level currency data to generate targeted, dynamic on-air marketing plans; roadmap moved from single-network daily automation (2015) to cross-channel campaign management (3Q15) to cross-platform/off-network optimization (2016). Reported 7-14% conversion lift and +44% cross-channel reach.

nodes.label: Big Knowledge
nodes.rationale: RSG Media's cross-platform analytics product family (Database/Modeling/Application strategy) covering Schedule Optimization, VOD Offer Management, Linear Offer Management, Rate Card Builder, Licensing Optimization and Digital Engagement apps — aimed at content acquisition, ad sales and marketing teams.

nodes.label: XPeranto (Data Integration/ETL Add-on)
nodes.rationale: RSG's proprietary high-transaction ETL product for integrating RightsLogic with external systems (Oracle, SQL Server, Sybase, DB2, FileMaker Pro, Excel/Access) — offered alongside the Web Services API as the two integration pathways into RightsLogic.

nodes.label: Ask NED
nodes.rationale: Real-time natural-English-language search/reporting feature ('type-ahead' plain-English queries) meant to democratize self-service reporting for business users who otherwise find traditional reporting tools overwhelming.

nodes.label: Planit
nodes.rationale: Cross-platform ad-sales planning tool addressing the inability to manage deals across networks/platforms; enables flexible product, pricing and market-strategy management across Promo Campaign Management, Ad Sales Management and Media Planning Optimization.

nodes.label: RSG Rights v4 Architecture
nodes.rationale: Ground-up rewrite of RightsLogic's rights/avails engine as a serverless, microservices architecture (React.js UI, Node.js app server, Redis caching, Kafka/Redis queues, PostgreSQL 13 + MongoDB, AWS Lambda) chosen to cut infrastructure cost, improve UX/scalability, and support self-service configuration across verticals (Content, Consumer Products, Studios, Digital) — motivated by prior versions' inability to flexibly onboard new asset hierarchies and rights types fast enough for a fragmenting distribution landscape.

nodes.label: 10 Spine Build Performance Rules
nodes.rationale: At spine scale the difference between seconds and hours/hung is always one of: a row-by-row write, a cross-join, or a non-deduped fan-out join — eliminate all three by construction. Proven by real failures: 903K-row executemany took 15h vs seconds set-based; 903K×863K cross-join hung >25min; dup tconsts caused 15-24x row inflation (84M-126M rows).

nodes.label: EIDR data gotchas (confirmed Jun 2026)
nodes.rationale: Column-name trap (ReleaseDate vs Release Date), multi-IMDB EIDR anthologies, type conflicts between Episode/Edition records and feature spine rows, AlternateResourceName foreign-title gap, and denominator confusion between PKID coverage (9.30%) and all-rows coverage (2.4%) all describe the same state — always name the denominator.

nodes.label: PARENTKEY-CONFIDENCE-002 (wikidata-fusion Path C, two-field rule)

nodes.label: SKILL-UPDATE-MEDIA-TITLERES-001 (OPUS↔IMDB↔EIDR validation set)
nodes.rationale: 138-row validation set proving primary-vs-primary title checks fail because localized primary titles drift independently across registries; resolve on IDs, anchor on original-language title, match the variant-set union.

nodes.label: Nielsen lag reality rule (multi-month gap = stalled feed)
nodes.rationale: A multi-month gap to the latest date is NOT normal reporting lag — it signals a source feed that stopped loading; confirm with SELECT max(BROADCAST_DATE) before assuming normal lag.
nodes.norm_label: nielsen lag reality rule (multi-month gap = stalled feed)

nodes.label: Relevance-Over-Volume Doctrine
nodes.rationale: Max intelligence = relevance per token, not volume of tokens; each agent reads core + its own domain slice only, never all 6 domains, because context dilution — every irrelevant fact is an attention tax that degrades decisions.

nodes.label: Memory Doctrine — Lifecycle (BRAIN-002, 2026-07-16)
nodes.rationale: Hot memory is an index of how to think and where to look, never a copy of what is; lifecycle is admit → reside → verified-refresh → demote → NEVER delete, so every eviction is a demotion with a tombstone, never a deletion.

nodes.label: Pointer-Not-Value Rule
nodes.rationale: Any queryable number/date/count/status referenced from a memory surface must be a pointer to its live source, never an inlined value — the 2026-07-16 WARM audit found stamped-but-rotted fields in voice.json/data.json and a duplicate design-token copy in product.json caused by inlining.

nodes.label: Verified-Refresh Rule
nodes.rationale: A refresh that re-stamps _updated without re-verifying each dated/counted field against its source is stamp fraud, not a refresh — sync jobs must verify-or-flag every such field.

nodes.label: Surface-Gate Lesson (2026-07-16 incident)
nodes.rationale: A gate that cannot be run on the current surface BLOCKS the action rather than being waived by good intentions — a claude.ai session defined an ls+grep verification gate it could not execute, then deleted slot detail anyway, requiring a retroactive verification task (BRAIN-002 P0.3).

nodes.label: Platform Naming Rules (LESSON-011–013, LESSON-019)
nodes.rationale: HOT must mean claude.ai's 30 slots only and WARM must mean CLAUDE_MEMORY.md/Upstash — conflating the two in an endpoint response caused a 136-line WARM bloat problem to misdiagnose as a HOT crisis; hygiene tasks also require full context window since compaction mid-operation truncates output silently.

nodes.label: Daemon Liveness Alert Design Rules (2026-06-09)
nodes.rationale: Lessons from the QUEUE-DRAIN-STALL false-positive incident: liveness alerts must be gated on work existence (AND with depth>0), catch blocks in daemons must log at WARN not swallow silently, startup must log critical config, and alert cooldown must be sized relative to the failure window — this incident's 10-min cooldown over an 8+ hour failure window produced 48 @here pings.

nodes.label: REBUILT FROM LIVE S3 (2026-07-16) note
nodes.rationale: Tables were regenerated from aws s3 ls on s3://sasmaster-2026/nielsen/{mit,amrld}/; prior invented row-count ranges and the fictional AMRLD T01–T08 taxonomy were removed — volume expectations and field semantics now live in nielsen-sme.

nodes.rationale: Covers silent-failure parsing traps (HALF_HR_ID=-1 as integer not 'PP', VCR viewing-type inflation, HH Universe Estimate expressed in thousands, DNA flag meaning suppressed not zero audience) and data-quality alert thresholds so pipelines don't silently corrupt joins.

nodes.label: §28 AMRLD BROADCAST_DATE is INTEGER YYYYMMDD
nodes.rationale: BROADCAST_DATE is stored as INT YYYYMMDD, not DATE type, so ISO-string filters silently return zero rows; WEEK_DATE is a proper DATE type; amrld_univ (REC71) uses EFF_DATE, not ST_EFF_DATE as the spec text claims.

nodes.label: §29 AMRLD Date Column Detection priority order
nodes.norm_label: §29 amrld date column detection priority order

nodes.label: §31 amrld_time_period_view: use original, not v2 (PERMANENT)
nodes.rationale: _v2 is an RSG client-scoped subset filtered to ~27 contracted networks (1.1B rows); the original covers the full 172-network national measurement universe (5.77B rows) — always use the original.

nodes.label: §32 MIT Table Naming Convention (War Room name vs Databricks table)
nodes.norm_label: §32 mit table naming convention (war room name vs databricks table)

nodes.label: §33 laapp_prod TMDB matches are fuzzy, not canonical
nodes.rationale: tmdb_gn_movie_match/tmdb_gn_series_match were built by searching TMDB's API by title+year and taking the first result — confirmed cross-type match error (a TV series matched to a TMDB movie ID); IMDB match tables (imdb_gn_movie_match, imdb_gn_series_match) are the trustworthy identity source instead, with zero overlap between the IMDB and TMDB match sets.
nodes.norm_label: §33 laapp_prod tmdb matches are fuzzy, not canonical

nodes.label: §34 laapp_prod Coverage Scope (client-scoped vs full-universe)
nodes.rationale: pcd_tn_gn_id and first_complete_match are RSG's contracted network set only, not full national; the IMDB match tables are full-universe, giving a confirmed coverage ceiling of ~9,966 parent keys wirable to Nielsen (72 movies + 9,894 series).

nodes.label: AMRLD has TWO layers — count both (WARROOM-DRILLDOWN-AMRLD-ETL-001)
nodes.rationale: A drill-down originally listed only raw REC* records and silently omitted the ETL amrld_time_period_view layer — a whole computed-table layer was missed; always check for a parallel computed/ETL prefix before declaring dataset coverage complete.
nodes.norm_label: amrld has two layers — count both (warroom-drilldown-amrld-etl-001)

nodes.label: LAAPP drill-down: dates-only, row-counts omitted (WARROOM-DRILLDOWN-LAAPP-001)
nodes.rationale: LAAPP drill-down dates were blank for months because the manifest generator had no generate_laapp() function — uniform-null meant a missing producer, not stale data; row counts are intentionally NULL because footer-SUM across ~5.84M tiny files is infeasible for a nightly job (build-discipline §39, no sampling).

nodes.rationale: ra_promo_prod is the sanctioned engine for all Nielsen pulls because the licensed Nielsen source lives in RSG's hive_metastore.laapp_prod and pulls must run where the entitlement is, until NIELSEN-LICENSE-001 gives SaSMaster its own feed; output is synced home via a SaSMaster-owned box so SaSMaster AWS creds are never parked in the RSG Databricks workspace.

nodes.label: PIL-SERVICE (v15 to v16 convergence)
nodes.rationale: Flips memory from a write-side discipline agents maintain into a service agents query at runtime, so agents become context-aware operators that consult the institution's whole memory before acting, rather than stateless executors.

nodes.label: Control Plane (governance hub)
nodes.rationale: Sits at the center of the flywheel, routing work and metering autonomy via fail-open/fail-closed policy, connecting by governance spokes to every rim stage; the dial shows share of outputs shipping with no human touch, rising as confidence sustains.

nodes.label: Wedge (single mission cell focus)
nodes.rationale: The entire six-stage loop is deliberately aimed at one mission cell rather than diffused across many, concentrating iteration.

nodes.label: Moat (currency-agnostic canonical layer)
nodes.rationale: Every turn of the flywheel deepens a currency-agnostic canonical data layer, compounding defensibility over time.

nodes.label: GATE (>=3x occurrence check)
nodes.rationale: Only patterns recurring three or more times are promoted (SLC); patterns under threshold are held rather than discarded, preventing premature skill sprawl.

nodes.label: !skill-approve (human gate)
nodes.rationale: Human-gated step that applies the change with backup, commit, and a 1-line rollback, and refuses blank/empty proposals — logging is autonomous but skill merges stay human-gated.

nodes.label: Progressive Disclosure (3-layer skill loading)
nodes.rationale: Metadata (~100 words) always loaded; SKILL.md (<500 lines) loaded on trigger; bundled resources loaded as needed — minimizes context cost while keeping full skill depth available.

nodes.label: Retro Computer-Head Mascot Brand Design
nodes.rationale: Hand-drawn sketch style, single-color blue line art on transparent/white background, depicting a humanoid figure with a vintage all-in-one computer (CRT monitor) as its head; conveys a playful, tech-personified brand identity for portal-v8, likely a scoped sub-brand or feature mascot distinct from core SaSMaster branding.

nodes.label: Portal Hero Section Visual Design
nodes.rationale: Wide-format photograph of a backpacker walking away from camera down a desert highway toward mountains, used as a full-bleed hero background; the wide aspect ratio and central vanishing-point composition leave clear space at top-left and right edges for overlaid UI chrome (nav/text), a common landing-page hero pattern signaling journey/exploration themes for portal-v8.
